defaults.permitted_development: Demolition in England is controlled by the GPDO and heritage legislation, not treated as a free general right. The route depends on what is being removed, whether Part 11 prior approval applies, and whether the site is listed, in a conservation area or otherwise protected. In rural settings, access, waste movements and the treatment of exposed edges after demolition can be the main concerns.

rules.height_rules: There is no demolition height allowance. The real question is the size, type and status of the structure and whether its removal falls within a prior approval route or needs a fuller application.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate depth rule. Partial demolition, demolition linked to rebuilding, or removal of only part of a structure must be assessed against the actual scope of works and any related development.
rules.boundary_rules: Party walls, adjoining land, hoardings, highway occupation, neighbour safety and the stability of nearby structures are often the most important boundary and site-management issues in a demolition proposal. In rural settings, access, waste movements and the treatment of exposed edges after demolition can be the main concerns.
rules.roof_rules: Removing a roof is not automatically a standalone permitted step. Once roof removal forms part of wider demolition, heritage, structural and weatherproofing issues can change the planning route.
rules.materials_rules: Salvage, asbestos handling, waste removal and making good exposed surfaces are key practical issues. Separate environmental, safety and building-control duties still apply even where the planning route is clear. In rural settings, access, waste movements and the treatment of exposed edges after demolition can be the main concerns.
